Essay p739.text: One degree below the common or the vulgar is the element of the base or gross, which differs from the common in being not only something negative, a simple lack of inspiration or nobleness, but something positive, marking coarse feelings, bad morals, and contemptible manners.

Essay p740a.text: The artist also may fall into a low style, not only by choosing ignoble subjects, offensive to decency and good taste, but moreover by treating them in a base manner. It is to treat a subject in a base manner if those sides are made prominent which propriety directs us to conceal, or if it is expressed in a manner that incidentally awakens low ideas.
Essay p740a.verification: maker compared scan; contributor identity, rights, independent alignment and kit gate pending

Essay p740b.text: No doubt there are cases where art itself may be allowed to produce base images: for example, when the aim is to provoke laughter.

Essay p741.text: This is not all: even in the serious and the tragic there are certain places where the low element can be brought into play. But in this case the affair must pass into the terrible, and the momentary violation of our good taste must be masked by a strong impression, which brings our passion into play. In other words, the low impression must be absorbed by a superior tragic impression.

research_update: A separate research reader compared four original 1877 pp.739–741 and Dole 1902 pp.262–264. Current 1902 wording matches print, but at p741 certain places omits the rarity of einige seltene Fälle and masked weakens ausgelöscht; p739 manners shifts Gesinnungen. The reader located a distinct 1845 translation by John Weiss covering all four places and inspected pp.268–271; this is a separate edition and does not identify the anonymous 1902 translator. Its historical text and contributor dates make it a priority candidate subject to print, semantic and territorial rights review. No formal kit review.

Essay p739.text: The Low stands yet one degree below the Common, and is distinguished from it by the fact, that it indicates not only something negative, not only a want of the spiritual and noble, but something positive, namely rudeness of feeling, bad manners and degraded sentiments.
Essay p739.note: Particularly recheck wording and punctuation on scan; OCR is damaged.

Essay p740a.text: In works of art also, the low may be apparent, not only by selecting low objects, which a sense of fitness and propriety forbids, but also by treating them in a low way. We so treat an object, either if we render that side conspicuous which propriety demands should be concealed, or if we give it an expression which suggests low, accessory representations.

Essay p740b.text: There are cases, it is true, where even in art the low may be allowed; there, namely, where its object is to excite laughter.

Essay p741.text: But there are a few cases even in the serious and tragic, where the low may be introduced. Yet then it must pass over into the fearful, and the momentary offence of taste must be counteracted by a powerful employment of emotion, and become as it were, swallowed up by a deeply tragical effect.
Essay p741.note: A few cases conveys limitation but not explicitly seltene; counteracted interprets ausgelöscht.
